editorial:
Imagine having to disappear from the world just to stay alive. You follow young Anne Frank, a bright and spunky girl who has to move into a secret attic with her family and a few others to hide from the Nazis. The vibe is very tense because you spend the whole movie worrying that one loud noise or one wrong move will give them away. It feels very personal, like you are reading her private thoughts while watching her try to grow up in a room where she cannot even open a window.

The acting is great, especially the girl playing Anne, who makes you really care about her dreams. The pacing is steady, though it can feel slow since they are stuck in one spot, but that just makes the danger feel more real. If you want a powerful story about hope and courage, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heartbreaking note when the secret hiding spot is finally discovered by the Nazis. You see the family and their friends get arrested and taken away in trucks. While the film does not show every detail of the camps, it makes it clear that Anne does not survive the war. The story wraps up by showing that her diary lived on, telling the world about her life and her hopes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves history or powerful true stories.
